items.q: The incidence of contrast-induced AKI is reduced by using:
items.exp: Contrast induced AKI: reduced incidence with low volume iso-osmolar contrast (iohexol/iopamidol). (Book p803)

items.q: Fill up: The iso-osmolar contrast agents named for reducing contrast-induced AKI are ______ and iopamidol.
items.exp: Low volume iso-osmolar contrast: iohexol/iopamidol. (Book p803)

items.q: Complete the aetiology of contrast-induced AKI — 1) Primary mechanism  2) Secondary mechanism  3) Histology … A) Medullary hypoxia  B) Vacuolar degeneration  C) Tubular injury beside the medullary hypoxia
items.exp: Contrast-induced AKI: medullary hypoxia is written as the primary mechanism (>>>) with tubular injury beside it, and the histology figure shows vacuolar degeneration. (Book p803)

items.q: In contrast-induced AKI, the creatinine first rises at what time?
items.exp: Contrast-induced AKI: creatinine ↑ in 24–48 hours, peaks in 3–5 days and normalises in 7–10 days. (Book p803)

items.q: Match the creatinine timeline of contrast-induced AKI — 1) Rise  2) Peak  3) Normal … A) 7–10 days  B) 3–5 days  C) 24–48 hours
items.exp: Contrast-induced AKI: creatinine ↑ in 24–48 hours, peaks at 3–5 days, normal in 7–10 days. (Book p803)

items.q: A patient who underwent contrast angiography 36 hours ago has a creatinine rise from 1.1 to 1.6 mg/dL. Which statement matches the book's course?
opts: The rise at 24–48 hours fits contrast-induced AKI, and the creatinine should peak at 3–5 days and normalise by 7–10 days
The creatinine should peak by 6 hours and normalise in 24 hours
The creatinine will never normalise in contrast nephropathy
A rise at 36 hours excludes contrast-induced AKI
items.exp: Contrast-induced AKI: creatinine ↑ in 24–48 hours, peak 3–5 days, normal in 7–10 days. (Book p803)

items.q: The management of contrast-induced AKI is:
opts: No treatment is required; prevention is by adequate hydration
items.exp: Management of contrast-induced AKI: Rx not required; prevention — adequate hydration. (Book p803)

items.q: The histology figure for contrast-induced AKI shows vacuolar degeneration. This corresponds to which aetiological mechanism?
opts: Immune complex deposition in the glomerulus
items.exp: The figure is labelled 'vacuolar degeneration in contrast induced AKI', the tubular injury that follows medullary hypoxia. (Book p803)

items.q: Contrast-induced AKI requires no specific drug treatment, and its prevention rests on adequate hydration.
opts: True, but only after alkalinisation of urine
items.exp: Management of contrast-induced AKI: Rx not required; prevention by adequate hydration. (Book p803)

items.q: All but one of the following statements about contrast-induced AKI are correct. Which is the odd one out?
opts: It is the commonest cause of hospital-acquired AKI
Creatinine returns to normal in 7–10 days
Aetiology is medullary hypoxia with tubular injury
items.exp: Pre-renal AKI is marked as the commonest cause of hospital AKI; contrast-induced AKI follows medullary hypoxia with tubular injury, peaking at 3–5 days and normalising by 7–10 days. (Book p803)
